subject: crystalBall
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: fortune teller's crystal ball on a claw stand.
Style: your choice. Pick an unexpected, striking visual style that suits this subject (not the obvious one), name it in a comment at the top of the module, and commit to it everywhere.
reasoning:
I'm brainstorming unexpected visual styles for the crystal ball on a claw stand, moving past the obvious mystic velvet look toward something more striking like constructivist poster art or other bold aesthetic directions.

I decide on Delft blue-and-white porcelain as the chosen style: glazed cobalt-on-white ceramic throughout the whole object, with the ball itself painted like a Delft tile showing a glowing swirl, eye, or stars rather than being transparent, keeping the palette largely monochrome with the glow as the main striking element.

Now I'm sizing the model: ball radius around 0.1, with a stepped round plinth base and a baluster pedestal roughly 0.13 radius and 0.05 height, aiming for a display-piece scale near 0.3 total height. I'm planning a stand made of claw-like legs curving up from the base to grip the ball, built as static swept geometry without joints since this is a static prop.

Writing leg sweep paths...

Still computing talon geometry...

I'm checking the cup geometry so the ball rests snugly without the rim poking outside the ball's radius at that height — adjusting the flare dimensions until the cup edge stays just inside the ball's cross-section.

Shaping the base profile for the lathe now, working out a lobed baluster foot that rises outward from the axis before tapering back — mapping radius and height coordinates point by point to get the Delft-style curve right.

Adjusting the cup rim shape and sinking the ball slightly so it rests properly, then thinking through leg placement — deciding between 3 or 4 legs, and settling on 3 legs positioned at 60°, 180°, and 300° so the front stays open for the ball's face.

Now I'm plotting out the actual leg geometry, working through the radius and height coordinates as each leg curves from its base foot up through the joint to where the talon attaches near the ball.

Working out the leg bulge path with knee at the widest point, then tapering through ankle to wrist. I'll add three talons per leg sweeping a short arc, with a knuckle sphere at the wrist and a radius profile that thickens at the knee and thins toward the foot.

Now I'm designing the foot as a flattened sphere pad rather than overcomplicating with extra scrollwork, then planning a Delft-style glaze function for the legs—white base with subtle blue-grey pooling in the lower areas to mimic painted ceramic scales.

I'm picking the actual palette: warm-cool white, a shade grey, and a few cobalt tones from deep to pale, then applying a scales pattern using the white base with cobalt edge lines for the leg texture. I'm now thinking through how to paint the talons, likely solid cobalt with a possible white tip accent.

For the base, I'm designing a paint function that places cobalt ring stripes and a dashed Delft-style border using the model's vertical position and angle around the piece, plus a glaze effect that darkens tones smoothstep-style underneath for shadow.

I'm also considering decal-based decoration for the plinth—small projected flat panels for motifs like cartouches with a moon and star, versus a procedural pattern approach, while planning SVG textures for the ball's face (eye, stars, swirling clouds) and other ornamental details.

Thinking about adding a ring of zodiac-like glyphs around the plinth using repeated decals, which means creating a few separate small textures (moon, sun, hand, eye) since one texture can't map differently per instance.

I decide against floating sparkle cards or an astrolabe-style halo ring since nothing should float freely in this design, keeping it simpler instead — favoring fish-scale textured legs, decaled plinth, and a scalloped rim of tiny pearl-like spheres placed along the plinth edge.

Now I'm adding acanthus-leaf extrusions at each leg's base and a fringe of 6-8 lotus petals around the pedestal column. For the ball itself, I'm working out a sphere with a wrapped equirectangular texture, calculating the seam placement and UV offsets so the front-facing side shows the correct portion of a glowing radial-gradient background image.

I'm designing the ball's surface in a Delft-tile style: a pale blue ground with cobalt swirl clouds and a central eye motif surrounded by rays and stars, so the glow reads as light shining through painted porcelain. I'm also considering adding a small white crescent highlight decal on the ball to break up the flat emissive look.

Since equirectangular mapping can't fake fresnel darkening at the rim, I'm tuning the emissive glow strength down to around 0.75 so the diffuse shading still shows through without clipping to pure white.

I also want the ground contrast with the cobalt art, so I'm shifting the ground gradient to mid-blue tones. For the texture, I'm working out that the front-facing hemisphere maps to the middle quarter of the equirect width given the rotation, and placing the eye detail accordingly.

Since the 2:1 equirectangular projection keeps pixels roughly square near the equator, a circle drawn in the texture stays a circle on the sphere there, so I don't need to stretch it. I'm sizing the iris and almond-shaped eye outline so they map to a reasonable arc width on the sphere, scaling down the half-width since my first estimate came out too wide relative to the ball's diameter.

Around the rest of the sphere I'll place complementary motifs — rays, four-point stars, crescent moons, and Delft-style hatched cloud swirls near the top and bottom, while keeping the polar 25% regions sparse since those distort most. I'm mapping out approximate x-positions for the moon, stars, and repeated back-view motifs across the texture width, accounting for the seam and the leg claws covering part of the surface.

I need a sun motif straddling the seam at x=0/400, so I'll draw duplicate halves at both edges so it reads as one continuous shape despite the viewBox clipping. Working out the rotation math confirms that with the [0,-90,0] orientation, the front of the model lines up with x=200 in the texture, and the middle longitude maps to the +Z direction after the -90° rotation about Y.

Tracing through the sphere's UV coordinates, I confirm the seam point at u=0.25 lands at −X after rotation, meaning when viewed from the front the texture reads left-to-right unmirrored—so x=100 corresponds to the viewer's left and x=300 to the right. I'm applying this same rotation logic to the ball-holding part, and now need to make sure the cobalt talons gripping it are positioned correctly too.

Checking that the legs at ±60° azimuth with their talon fan spanning ±14° don't block the visible eye, which sits within ±40°—confirmed clear. Now I'm planning out the decorative elements: deciding against a dew claw or halo ring, and sketching the texture list, starting with the main ball texture and a set of Delft-tile icon medallions (moon, sun, hand-with-eye, star) each framed in a circular cartouche.

I'm debating whether to add tiny floating sparkle cards orbiting the ball—star-shaped cobalt/white twinkles—but second-guessing since the rule says nothing should float free of the body, so I'm weighing whether this breaks that constraint. I'll likely drop the free-floating sparkles and instead keep decorative elements attached, while still including a glint decal on the ball and a petal-vein paint for any extruded lotus petals.

I'm checking that mix, noise, paint, resolve, rgb, smoothstep, and cells are all available as exports from the SDK so I can use them for the glaze shading function.

Writing lighting function...

Writing scale pattern logic...

For the talons, I want a cobalt body with an ivory tip, so I'll use a sweep function that returns white near the tip and cobalt elsewhere, keeping the leg's lower section unchanged for now.

Now I'm setting up the lathe-based plinth paint using height and angle, mixing white with a pale blue-gray noise base color and adding cobalt bands at specific height ranges, with a helper function to check if a point falls within a band.

Still writing lathe profile...

Reworking the plinth drum to be taller so the Delft decals have more room, adjusting the radius and height values, then continuing the profile curve up toward the column rim and ball joint.

Now I'm sketching the cabriole leg, starting it sunk into the plinth top and flaring the knee outward beyond the plinth radius for a graceful curve down toward the wrist point.

I'm computing the wrist position relative to the ball at a -32° angle and checking the midpoint distance stays clear of the ball's radius so the leg doesn't overlap it. Then I'm planning an acanthus leaf foot shape extruded outward at the leg's base.

Switching to a lotus petal ring around the column instead—8 extruded petals plus 3 acanthus leaves at the leg roots, with each petal shaped to lean outward from the column's radius...

Writing petal paint logic...

Actually, maybe it's simpler to keep the petal flat white and add the cobalt rim separately with a slightly larger extrude layered behind it, which would avoid needing per-petal wall-normal math entirely.

I'm also thinking about richness at the leg roots — maybe acanthus leaf scrollwork, though that could be skipped for simplicity. Instead I'll focus on adding dragon-claw spikes along the outer dorsal edge of each leg using the sweep's angle parameter to position them.

I'm computing spike placements by taking points along the leg path and offsetting outward along a radial direction, then placing graduated spikes at a few t-values with cobalt-white paint for a dragon-spur effect. I also want to add a knuckle sphere near the knee for articulation detail.

For the wrist I'm placing a small sphere with cobalt rings, then working out the three talons per leg using azimuth offsets and a path that curves from the wrist down to the tip, making sure the talon radius stays slightly embedded in the ball's surface so the grip looks natural rather than floating above it.

For splay, I'm having each talon's azimuth diverge more toward the tip than the root, giving the claws a fanned-out look as they curve around the sphere. Now I'm skipping the rear dewclaw and ball pole details, and moving to the plinth's medallion decals, sizing and positioning them at the leg azimuths around the drum.

For placement, I'm putting three larger medallions (hand/eye, moon, sun) at the front and two back azimuths, with three smaller star decals rotated between them beneath the leg roots where the drum stays visible. I'm computing each decal's surface point and outward direction for the lathe decal function, keeping segment count and curvature modest given the small width relative to the drum radius.

For the beaded trim around the top edge, I'm planning a ring of two-tone beads merged into fewer draw calls rather than placing dozens of separate sphere parts, generating positions around a circle at the right radius and height and alternating colors before merging geometries by color group.

I'm placing the glint decal by finding the hit point on the ball surface at that azimuth/elevation, using the surface normal as direction and world up for orientation. I'll make it opaque white with full glow since the base color is too pale for contrast, then add a second smaller glint dot at the lower right.

The glow effect clones the mesh and sets an emissive map matching the texture, so applying it to the ball's textured part should work fine. Now I'm designing the ball's SVG texture in Delft style, starting with a vertical gradient sky background and sketching the swirling cloud strokes typical of that aesthetic.

I'm writing a helper function to generate spiral-shaped cloud paths, with wraparound offsets so swirls near the seam edges tile correctly, then planning the layout of eye and other facial elements across the texture.

Still writing the eye details... iris, pupil, highlight, lashes, dotted rings, and hatching, then sketching positions for sparkle stars and a crescent moon, checking they stay within the visible bounds near the almond eye shape.

I'm planning the Delft border rows with scalloped arcs and calculating stroke widths relative to canvas scale, then sketching the medallion tile icons—a pale wash circle with a cobalt double ring framing symbols like a palm with an eye in the center.

Still writing hand icon paths...

For the moon, I realize using a mask is cleaner: a full circle with a black offset circle cut out to create the crescent shape, which is reliable in SVG rendering.

Now I'm sketching the other icon textures: a sun with triangular rays, an eight-point star burst via a helper function, plus a medallion frame wrapper with a pale outer ring and dashed inner circle for consistent card styling. I'm also thinking through how the sparkle/glow card variant should look, with a soft star shape and cobalt outline for a subtle shine effect.

Checking overall proportions now: ball diameter lands around 0.3m (a hefty 20cm crystal ball), sitting on a 0.15m radius base, with legs sinking cleanly into the plinth so everything touches the floor properly. I'm also working out how the glow/sweep helper functions handle part and card meshes so the texture application stays consistent across all pieces.

Adding decorative rings now — a cobalt collar torus near the cup's top, plus gadrooned torus rings at the plinth and drum sections for extra ornamental detail, then planning a row of lotus petals wrapping around the column base.

Checking the ball position confirms the petal tip stays clear below it. Now I'm reconsidering the lean angle and base placement against the column's widening profile, testing a base at y=0.06 with radius 0.071 and tracing the tip outward to see where it lands relative to the column surface.

Let me simplify the column shape entirely—a cleaner flared profile with a cup-like curve—and set the petals on the shoulder leaning inward slightly so they cling closely to the column surface, checking that the tip radius matches the column radius at that height.

Finalizing the profile coordinates now, making sure the rim curves inward at the top and verifying the resting ball clears the cup's interior without clipping through the rim.

I'll use 24 segments with no smoothing for the lathe geometry, and I'm now writing the paint banding function that colors the piece based on height—cobalt bands near the foot and rim, white glaze elsewhere.

Writing color banding logic...

Still defining color bands...

Writing shading and coordinate helper functions...

Writing leg sweep taper...

Setting the leaf thickness and tangent/up directions so the extrusion stays geometrically consistent, then planning a shared leafPaint helper function for coloring and figuring out which face counts as the front for the extrude.

For sparkles, I'm thinking through using double-sided star cards positioned around the ball at a fixed radius, oriented with upward frames and shifted so their bottom edge aligns, then adding a glow effect. I'm also starting to set up decal placement on the plinth with position and direction parameters.

Writing decal placement code...

I also need to check decal orientation and texture mirroring, confirm the lathe's flat-shaded facets are wide enough for readable decals, and handle the ball's glint decal using a raycast hit that could return null, plus settle on sphere segment counts for a smooth surface.

Now I'm sketching the torus geometry for the drum rings, rotating them into the XZ plane, and considering whether to add bead details or ankle rings before finalizing the component layout and exporting the metadata object.

Writing style comment and code...

Still defining color-mixing functions...

Writing base paint logic...

Resizing the medallion slightly to avoid colliding with the corner triangles, then moving to the shoulder region—defining concentric COB and glaze rings by radius, plus bead details sitting on the ring near the leg roots.

For the column, I'm deciding between flute lines and a petal ring for coverage between y .056–.092, concluding the petals dominate so flutes become redundant—better to rely on bands above the petal tips and distinct rim bands near the top, differentiating COB and COB_L by narrow y-ranges as the geometry transitions into the rim.

Inside the dish I'm blending washed and cobalt-light tones radially from center, with a concentric cobalt ring near r~0.04 for a simple decorative motif, then returning the lit color with normal shading.

For the talon coloring function, I'm mapping parametric position along the claw to color—dark cobalt base, cobalt mid-section, and a pale near-white tip for a bone-claw look.

Now I'm placing the leg spikes using azimuth angles at 60°, 180°, and 300° for symmetric triangular placement, then building each talon as a fanned catmull-rom path with offset azimuths and tapering radius so the claw tip comes to a point near the ball's surface.

Checking that the inner surface of each talon clears the ball radius by a few millimeters — I'm shaving the taper radii slightly so the gap stays consistent at around 2.5mm, then positioning a wrist knuckle sphere at the base of each leg to match where the talon path ends.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for the decorative elements: one generating star point coordinates, another building a spiral path string by stepping outward with a shrinking radius and rotating angle — this will give the cloud/mist swirl a magical, billowing look in the Delft style.

Writing SVG assembly code...

Adding sparkle stars and small flanking sun/moon shapes near the eyes, plus a bigger decorative sun with rays and a face in the back corner.

Writing eye ray and almond shape code...

Writing medallion SVG function...

Writing texture SVGs...

Now I'm placing decals around the drum: hand icon at the front azimuth, moon and sun at the other two thirds, with smaller stars filling the gaps, making sure the leg roots clear the decal tops. For the pearl ring, I'm spacing them every 12 degrees while skipping positions too close to the leg attachment points.

Then I'm positioning the petals around the column—computing their base radius against the column's taper profile, angling them inward with a lean vector, and checking that the petal tips leave a small clearance gap above the shoulder so nothing clips into the column surface.

Writing petal shape outline...

To avoid risky imports, I'll define my own local union type for outline points instead of relying on the builder's exported type. For the leg-root leaf, I'm placing it at the same radial position as the petal using tangent and outward-up blended directions, with a sharp tip, tighter thickness, and matching paint treatment.

Now I'm adding two smaller flanking leaves per leg, rotated roughly ±14° in azimuth and scaled down to about 0.7, giving three leaves per leg (nine extrusions total alongside the ten petals) while checking that leaf placement near the knee doesn't excessively overlap the leg geometry.

Tracing the leg's curve through the knee more precisely, I find the outer surface radius grows to about .192 near the knee bend, which matches well with where I want the leaf tip to land tangent to the leg. Checking the base position too — leg center radius at y=.046 is about .14 with thickness .018, giving an outer edge at .158, which lines up nicely with my leaf base placement.

Now I'm deciding where to put spurs — thinking skipping the back-side spur idea since it's not very visible, and instead considering small knuckle bumps or dew-claw spikes near the wrist pointing downward-outward instead.

I'm checking the wrist's position against the foot ball to make sure the dewclaw placement doesn't collide, then tallying up all the parts across legs, petals, plinth, decals, tori, beads, and other decorative elements to get a rough total part count for the model.

I'm still well below the target range, so I'm considering adding more detail: segmenting talons into base sleeves plus claws, adding scale plates along the legs, and placing knuckle ring tori at intervals along the leg sweep oriented to the tangent direction.

Still working out leg band placement...

I'm adding small details like toe pad spheres at talon bases and cobalt accent dots on petals, keeping the plinth bottom simple with no extra feet. Total part count is landing somewhere around 110-150, which feels like enough richness without being overly strict about hitting an exact number.

Setting up imports from the builder library...

Writing geometry helper functions...

Writing ball SVG and rays...

Still writing SVG elements...

Adding glow decals and sparkle positioning...

Checking clearance confirms the sparkle stays clear of the leg geometry. Now I'm defining the three legs at phi angles 60/180/300, building each leg's path through a sequence of radial points up to the wrist, then sweeping tapered tube radii along that curve to form clawed limbs.

I'm interpolating leg radius smoothly across the sweep, placing small torus rings as joint accents along the path with orientation matching the tangent direction, adding a flattened sphere foot near the base of each leg, and a knuckle sphere at the wrist.

Now I'm adding dewclaw spikes angled outward and down from the wrist, computing their base position and direction with vector helpers, and checking their placement relative to the ball's radius so they sit naturally near the joint without overlapping the body.

For the talons, I'm building three toe curves using Catmull-Rom splines through points that shrink in radius toward the tip, spacing them angularly so they fuse at the root but spread apart toward the tips without clipping into each other.

Then I'm adding a small toe pad sphere near the base of each talon, and decorative beads around the top ring at regular angular intervals, skipping positions too close to the leg attachments.

Placing a few more decorative tori along the drum's rim and shoulder, plus a cup collar torus higher up to add structural detail to the plinth.

I'm setting up the lathe call for the plinth using the base profile, axis, and segment count, then arranging decal medallions (hand, moon, sun, and three stars) around the ring at specific angles and sizes before looping through to place each decal.

Defining decal placements...

Writing a paint function for leaf/petal shapes that checks surface normals against the blade's thickness axis and uses coordinate thresholds to decide between cobalt accents and a pale-to-white gradient fill.

Writing paint function logic...

Still mapping out color zones for rings and radial bands...

I'm double-checking edge cases for the drum shape, like the wall boundaries and the sloped lip bevel where the surfaces meet, confirming the lit function and types handle both string and Rgb color values correctly. Now I'm moving on to the leg paint section.

I'm writing the leg's cellular glaze pattern, blending a base wash with darker cobalt tones along cell edges, then confirming the cells function is properly exported and verifying how sparkle cards get randomized placement using rng-seeded variation.

Now I'm drafting the SVG markup for the hand icon, with cobalt-stroked fingers and a palm shape outlined in white and cobalt, plus a small dot for a detail mark -- then moving on to similar inner icons for the moon-with-star and sun motifs.

I'm verifying the lathe profile points don't self-intersect near the column, tracing through the coordinates to confirm the shape closes cleanly along the axis. The sphere geometry's segment counts should keep the triangle count reasonable, so I'm finalizing the details including typing for the decals' size property.

For the glint decal placement, I'm setting the hit-based position with a small size and considering the roll rotation to match the crescent orientation. I'll skip adding extra tiny decorations to keep things simple, then just need to make sure the array types are explicit tuples so the destructuring in the map callback type-checks correctly.
